title: Solomon's Apostasy and Jeroboam's Sin
english: …Receiving one's own examples as members, we barely ascend to weak thoughts about God. The queen of Sheba, etc. From Cyril's homily on Luke. A barbarian woman, having overcome long distances, became more excellent through her longing, not to collect money, but to hear Solomon's wisdom, speaking in parables and riddles, and describing human virtues and vices. Then Solomon built a high place for the idol of Chemosh in Moab.

What would be the worst of such outrageous sins, giving honor and love to demonic herds, rather than to the one true God, and building temples for them with stones and wood? The Lord was angry with Solomon, etc. What then was the command given to him and to all men under the law, not to marry foreign women? For he said, 'You shall not give your daughter to his son, and you shall not take his daughter for your son. For he will turn your son away from me, and having gone, he will serve other gods.' (Deuteronomy 7:3-4) Forgetting this command, he became entangled with the daughters of foreign tribes. Since, he says, having done nothing regarding the given command, having slipped into apostasy by serving foreign gods, and having given my creation, which is my servant, to her, knowing that I have given her my honor and glory, which is mine alone and most fitting, and I will tear your kingdom apart and give it to your servant, so that you may learn from what has happened to you.

For since Solomon, though he was very wise, was overcome by desires for women, he utterly ruined the kingdom of God, setting up idols and giving them the honor and glory that belong to Him alone; for this reason, God threatened to tear his kingdom apart, being equally angry with those, according to what is written in the prophet Ezekiel: 'As you have done, so it shall be done to you; your recompense shall be returned to your head.' (Ezekiel 7:27) And the king consulted and went and made two calves.

Jeroboam became a snare to those of Israel, showing the rising up of the kingship of men, and departing from the kingship of God through prophets. For behold, Jeroboam provoked me, the Lord, by innovating calves and having placed my dignity upon them. And again: Jeroboam thought in his beginnings to fulfill the established customs upon the calves, to set up with his own inventions the glory due to God, so that he might have the kingdom securely, but he would deprive God, just as from his own. And Naboth had a vineyard. Cyril posits that Isaiah is a type of the Israel here. But those considering this, of whom Ahab is a type, I desired to have him, but they did not persuade him to betray the excellent vineyard of his father to them, so that they might also convert it into a vegetable garden, teaching the commandments of human teachings, and watering…
translator_notes: The text begins and ends mid-sentence; '…receiving' and '…watering' are edge fragments.
The fragment 'ποτίζοντες' (watering) is left uncompleted as the source text cuts off.
baehrens: PG 69; Fragmenta in Regum b03 rem early

title: The Corruption of Zeal Through Worldly Distraction
english: For these people have not even learned to rebuke, as if they had never properly advised God at any time. Having taken the silver, as it were, Cyril thus bears witness, and so too Christ in the holy Gospels declares: Carry neither money bag, nor sack, nor sandals; and greet no one along the way. For one must advance upon the work with a direct and unwavering impulse, nor even return a blessing to one who offers it. Indeed, the harm to zeal lies in turning away toward others, and to spend the time owed to the proclamations idly on trivial matters, nor to indulge in leisurely delay for the sake of useless friendships.

Fragmenta in libros Regum 69.693.31 to Fragmenta in libros Regum: And they inherited Samaria. Thus Cyril: These, having obtained the lot, dwelt in the land of the Samaritans, and perhaps became fathers of children somewhere; and having inclined to the customs of the Jews, they fortified the approaches against the lions. From them arose the Sarasars and the Arbaseser, the latter also called king, through whom this very day those transplanted in Samaria from the Persians are led. Hezekiah, son of Ahaz, king of Judah, began to reign. Thus Cyril: He had advanced to both glory and at once strength to this point, so as to domineer the nations dwelling around Judah, and indeed to impose many taxes upon them. Then shortly afterward: Then he suffered something human, for from excessive delicacy, and overcome by the height of his good reputation, in some way he grew proud, and being held fast by the disease of superiority, even he himself had raised up the divine law against him.

title: The Folly of Idolatry and the Majesty of the True God
english: It is necessary for one to also crown oneself with the dignity of the divine priesthood, for he dared to enter the divine temple himself and to burn incense to God, carefully attending to the customary observances.
Because of this act, he was immediately struck with leprosy and became utterly dishonored, for according to the law, anyone seized by leprosy is considered unclean.

The barbarian, having both understanding and speech, perhaps thought himself lord of earth and heaven, creator of all things, and God, because he served one of the false gods, and so he mocked, saying, 'Where is the God of Math?' and 'They have taken Samaria from my hand?'
It is the custom of those who do not know God to mock at times the hope of the saints, and they would not dare to speak against God, claiming to dare do so.

He did not overlook the fact that the false gods are the work of human hands, but the one who truly exists by nature, made by no one, has himself brought forth into being the things that were not at all.

Come down, Samaria, for God is withholding his aid, and as I said before, even if none of the gods spoken of by the Greeks has saved his own, this avails nothing toward God, who truly exists by nature and is great.
For those gods made by human art have been weak, unable even to be seen, but he rules over all things, being Lord of the powers.
Having neglected his own concerns, he tore his garments around him, grieving for God and seeking vindication, and he put on sackcloth and entered the house of the Lord.
The reason for tearing his garments was that it was a custom among the Jews to do so in the face of divine reproaches, as also occurred under Caiaphas in the Gospels.
He said, 'I cut off the height of his cedar,' referring to the kingdom of Judah, which he was about to lift to a great height.
And he said, 'I will place my hooks in your nostrils, and my bridle in your lips,' meaning that he would restrain them from speaking boldly.

Even if he did not associate with the multitude because of the stated reason, for which Pharaoh also kept watch as a spectator of the remaining Egyptians being punished, yet he found his own sons to be murderers, having come upon his own native land.
And he said, 'I will defend this city for my own sake,' which is fitting for God who truly is, and therefore he will do these things for his own sake, not because those who are helped are worthy.
An angel of the Lord went out and struck 185,000 in the camp of the Assyrians, and the war was loosed, but the threats fled with the dangers.

The inhabitants of Jerusalem will speak great things, rejoicing, saying, 'You have turned my mourning into joy for me,' for the mourning was great because of the multitude of those fighting, and great has become the joy because of the multitude of those who have fallen (Psalm 30:11).
